SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.937532, -81.13206 (Approximated from premise)
Report Description///NEEC INCIDENT NOTIFICATION: BARN FIRE WITH DOUSE WATER AND MANURE RUNOFF./// BARN IS BLAZING CURRENTLY AND THERE ARE A NUMBER OF TRUCKS APPLYING WATER. FD COMMANDER ADVISED RUNOFF WOULD BE PARTICULATES AND MANURE FROM THE COW PENS, NOT MANURE STORAGE. IT IS DRAINING TO THE SOUTH AND THERE IS A CATCHBASIN ON THE PROPERTY WHERE EVERYTHING IS DRAINING INTO. CALLER DOES NOT KNOW THE INFRASTRUCTURE. THERE IS A POND TO THE SE OF THE PROPERTY SO HE THINKS IT MIGHT GO TO THE PRIVATE POND ON THE PROPERTY. NOT AWARE OF ANY EVACUATIONS OR SHELTER IN PLACE. SMOKE IS GOING STRAIGHT UP, GREY. THIS IS NOT THE FIRST TIME THERE HAS BEEN A FIRE AT THE PROPERTY. THEY HAVE JUST USED WATER NOT ANY FOAM. CALLER IS NOT AWARE OF ANY SENSITIVE RECEPTORS OR WATERCOURSES NEARBY. THERE ARE SOME MUNICIPAL DRAINS IN THE VICINITY BUT HE IS NOT FAMILIAR WITH WHERE THE CATCHBASIN ON THE PROPERTY IS LEADING. HIS BOSS WAS ASKING SINCE IT IS DIFFICULT TO SEE THE SITE IF IT WOULD BE BEST TO MEET MECP ON SITE FIRST THING IN THE MORNING. I ASKED IF THERE IS ANY WAY TO REDUCE OFFSITE RUNOFF AND HE SAID NOT REALLY DUE TO THE WATER FLOW. THE CITY ADVISED THERE IS NOT MUCH THEY CAN DO AT THIS TIME. I REQUESTED THAT HE REACH OUT TO THE FD TO GET THE SITE CONTACT TO ASK WHERE THE DRAIN GOES. IF THEY CAN FIND OUTFALLS THERE COULD BE POTENTIAL TO PUT IN SOME HAYBALES OR OTHER FILTERS TO REDUCE IMPACTS.

THIS IS NOT THE FIRST TIME THERE HAS BEEN A FIRE AT THE PROPERTY. THEY HAVE JUST USED WATER NOT ANY FOAM. CALLER IS NOT AWARE OF ANY SENSITIVE RECEPTORS OR WATERCOURSES NEARBY. THERE ARE SOME MUNICIPAL DRAINS IN THE VICINITY BUT HE IS NOT FAMILIAR WITH WHERE THE CATCHBASIN ON THE PROPERTY IS LEADING. HIS BOSS WAS ASKING SINCE IT IS DIFFICULT TO SEE THE SITE IF IT WOULD BE BEST TO MEET MECP ON SITE FIRST THING IN THE MORNING. I ASKED IF THERE IS ANY WAY TO REDUCE OFFSITE RUNOFF AND HE SAID NOT REALLY DUE TO THE WATER FLOW. THE CITY ADVISED THERE IS NOT MUCH THEY CAN DO AT THIS TIME. I REQUESTED THAT HE REACH OUT TO THE FD TO GET THE SITE CONTACT TO ASK WHERE THE DRAIN GOES. IF THEY CAN FIND OUTFALLS THERE COULD BE POTENTIAL TO PUT IN SOME HAYBALES OR OTHER FILTERS TO REDUCE IMPACTS.

Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** THE M/V ANGELIA B, VN:631713, REPORTED A HYDRAULIC OIL LEAK IN THE RUDDER COMPARTMENT AT APPROX. 0715, 03DEC13, WHILE MOORED AT THE EVANSVILLE MARINE SERVICE (EMS) FACILITY. THE TANKERMAN ON DUTY REPORTED IT TO ME, THE SAFETY COORDINATOR FOR EMS. AT IT'S LARGEST, THE SHEEN WAS APPROX. 15' X 2', AND WAS SILVERY/GRAY IN COLOR. BEST ESTIMATES ARE THAT LESS THAN 1 PINT WAS RELEASED INTO THE RIVER. ATTEMPTS WERE MADE TO CONTAIN THE SPILL, WHICH REMAINED TRAPPED BEHIND THE VESSEL FOR SEVERAL MINUTES, BUT THE SHEEN WAS NOT ABSORBED BY THE OIL PADS. THE MECHANIC ON DUTY BOARDED THE VESSEL AND FOUND THE CAUSE. THE LEAK IS NOW CONTAINED, BUT HAS NOT BEEN REPAIRED AT THIS TIME. EXPECTED REPAIRS SHOULD BE COMPLETE WITHIN THE HOUR.

THE SHEEN EXTENDED APPROXIMATELY 3.5 NM WEST OF RACCOON ISLAND, WITH THE WIDEST AREA APPROXIMATELY REACHING .7 NM ACROSS. A SECOND, SMALLER SEGMENT OF POSSIBLE OIL AND VERY FAINT SHEEN WAS OBSERVED ABOUT 2.6 NM NE OF THE ISLAND. WINDS WERE FROM E ABOUT 5 KT, WHICH SUPPORTS A WESTERN TRAJECTORY FROM THE LAST REPORTED LOCATION OF POSSIBLE OIL AND THE FEATHERING PATTERN OBSERVED.

Report Description
WHILE LOADING A RAILCAR WITH GAVILON-OWNED YELLOW GREASE FROM A TRUCK ON DECEMBER 16, 2011. APPROXIMATELY 10 TO 15 GALLONS OF YELLOW GREASE WERE RELEASED TO THE GROUND DUE TO AN OVERFILL OF A RAILCAR. RESTAURANT SERVICES PERSONNEL REPORTEDLY STOPPED THE RELEASE FROM ENTERING A NEARBY STORM DRAIN AND CLEANED UP THE RELEASE. WHEN GAVILON PERSONNEL VISITED THE SITE ON 12/21/2011, IT APPEARED THAT SOME OF THE YELLOW GREASE COULD HAVE ENTERED A NEARBY STORM DRAIN. GAVILON IS CALLING A LOCAL RESPONSE COMPANY TO CLEAN OUT THE STORM DRAIN IN CASE IT HAD YELLOW GREASE IN IT. NO PRECIPITATION WAS NOTED BETWEEN THE TIME OF THE RELEASE AND THE DISCOVER BY GAVILON (I..E, THE GREASE MAY NOT HAVE BEEN FLUSHED TO A NAVIGABLE WATERWAY).

WHILE LOADING A RAILCAR WITH GAVILON-OWNED YELLOW GREASE FROM A TRUCK ON DECEMBER 16, 2011. APPROXIMATELY 10 TO 15 GALLONS OF YELLOW GREASE WERE RELEASED TO THE GROUND DUE TO AN OVERFILL OF A RAILCAR. RESTAURANT SERVICES PERSONNEL REPORTEDLY STOPPED THE RELEASE FROM ENTERING A NEARBY STORM DRAIN AND CLEANED UP THE RELEASE. WHEN GAVILON PERSONNEL VISITED THE SITE ON 12/21/2011, IT APPEARED THAT SOME OF THE YELLOW GREASE COULD HAVE ENTERED A NEARBY STORM DRAIN. GAVILON IS CALLING A LOCAL RESPONSE COMPANY TO CLEAN OUT THE STORM DRAIN IN CASE IT HAD YELLOW GREASE IN IT. NO PRECIPITATION WAS NOTED BETWEEN THE TIME OF THE RELEASE AND THE DISCOVER BY GAVILON (I..E, THE GREASE MAY NOT HAVE BEEN FLUSHED TO A NAVIGABLE WATERWAY).

properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 977627
Incident Time: 2011-05-22 21:00:00
Nearest City: Rawlins, WY
Incident Type: STORAGE TANK
Material: OIL: CRUDE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: NADEL AND GUSSMAN ROCKIES
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 3360 gallons
THIS REPORT IS A FOLLOW UP TO NRC INCIDENT REPORT # 977399. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION HAS BECOME AVAILABLE SUBSEQUENT TO INITIAL REPORT. THE SOURCE IS BELIEVED TO BE AN IMPAIRED PRODUCTION UNIT AT THE TANK BATTERY. FROM THE SUSPECTED SOURCE, THE OIL TRAVELED APPROXIMATELY 1,650 FEET DOWN GRADIENT TO THE SOUTHEAST AND ENTERED A TRIBUTARY TO EMIGRANT CREEK. THE PRIMARY IMPACT CONSISTED OF APPROXIMATELY AT 29,535 SQUARE FEET OF STAINED SOILS, DISTRESSED VEGETATION, AND SHEEN ON WATER SURFACE ALONG THE NORTHERN EDGE OF THE TRIBUTARY. IMPACTS (E.G., STAINED SOILS, DISTRESSED VEGETATION, AND SHEEN ON WATER SURFACE) WERE ALSO OBSERVED ALONG EMIGRANT CREEK APPROXIMATELY 3 MILES PAST BRIDGER PASS ROAD. SOME SPOTS OF OIL AND DISTRESSED VEGETATION WERE ALSO NOTED BELOW AN ACCESS ROAD SOUTH OF THE FACILITY ALL THE WAY TO THE CONFLUENCE. THE RELEASE WAS REPORTED TO THE BLM BY A PRIVATE INDIVIDUAL. THE WYOMING DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY AND A REPRESENTATIVE FROM THE BLM ARE ALREADY ON THE SCENE. TETON RESERVOIR IS LOCATED DOWNGRADIENT OF THE RELEASE AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS ARE UNDERWAY TO PREVENT MIGRATION OF THE RELEASED MATERIALS TO THIS RESERVOIR.

THE CALLER STATED THAT IT IS UNKNOWN HOW MUCH OF THAT ESTIMATED AMOUNT MAY HAVE MADE ITS WAS INTO THE CANAL. THE CANAL LEADS TO THE UMATILLA RIVER AND THE CALLER SUSPECTS THE MATERIAL MADE ITS WAY THERE. THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE IS CURRENTLY UNKNOWN AND UNDER INVESTIGATION. CURRENTLY THE TRAIN IS STOPPED AT MILE POST (200).

RP STATED THE PLANT WHERE THE SOIL IS BEING TRANSPORTED FROM IS IN SUWANEE COUNTY, FL (EXACT ADDRESS UNKNOWN). RP STATED IT IS UNKNOWN IF THE TOP SOIL HAS ANY POLLUTANTS OR CONTAINMENTS BUT IS BELIEVED TO CONTAIN AN UNKNOWN FUEL OIL. RP STATED THE FACILITY WAS BUILT IN THE 1950S OR 60S.

THE CALLER FURTHER REPORTED THE SOURCE WAS UNKNOWN. THE VENTURA HARBOR PATROL RESPONDED TO THE AREA AND OBSERVED A LIGHT SHEEN ON THE WATER COVERING A DISTANCE OF APPROXIMATELY 20' WIDE BY 60' LONG AND APPEARED TO BE ISOLATED AND MORE THAN LIKELY OCCURRED EARLIER IN THE MORNING. NO FURTHER ACTIONS WERE TAKEN AND THE AREA WILL BE MONITORED PERIODICALLY TO DETERMINE IF THIS WILL BE A REGULAR PROBLEM.

properties.summary: Incident Type: VESSEL - NRC Report ID: 995183 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party:
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 995183
Incident Time: 2011-11-10 15:00:00
Nearest City: Nome, AK
Incident Type: VESSEL
Material: OIL: DIESEL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 64.495347, -165.407076 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 5 gallons
Report Description
NOME HARBOR EXPERIENCED VERY HIGH WATER (+10 MLLW) AROUND 1700 ON 9 NOV 2011. TUG RUSTLER WAS MOORED IN SOUTHEAST CORNER OF HARBOR STERN TO A GRAVEL BANK. AS WATER ROSE THE VESSEL WAS PULLED BACK TOWARD THE BANK TO GROUND FOR WINTER ICE PERIOD. THE VESSEL WAS APPARENTLY LEFT UNATTENDED AS THE WATERS RECEDED AND AS IT GROUNDED IT WAS TOO FAR OFF THE SHEET PILE WALL TO REMAIN REASONABLY UPRIGHT (WITH ONLY A SLIGHT LIST TO PORT) AND LEANED WELL BEYOND A 45 DEGREE ANGLE. THE PORT BOW AND MID-SHIP GUNNELS ARE UNDERWATER AND SOME OIL PRODUCT HAS BEEN RELEASED FROM EQUIPMENT AND TOOLS THAT WERE ON THE DECK. OWNER HAS BEEN NOTIFIED TO RESPOND. SMALL CHUNKS OF ICE SURROUND THE VESSEL AND THE WATER IS CALM THEREFORE DO NOT EXPECT A LOT OF SPREADING AT THIS POINT. THIS COULD CHANGE IF ANOTHER STORM SYSTEM APPROACHED THE REGION. WILL CONTINUE TO WORK WITH RESPONSIBLE PARTY.

Report Description/// NOAA/NESDIS MPSR ISSUED FOR: GULF OF AMERICA /// POSSIBLE, UNCONFIRMED OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. REPORT DATE: 03-12-2026 REPORT TIME: 0100 UTC REGION: GULF OF AMERICA SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: SHIP SHOAL 42 IMAGE DATE: 03-11-2026 IMAGE TIME: 1716 UTC DATA SOURCE: PLANETSCOPE MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 3 METER LOCATION: 29°05'23" N/90°45'33" W AREA: 3.21 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THESE OIL SLICKS WERE BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH NOAA RESPONSE LINK HOTLINE #11125 NOW IN THE SHIP SHOAL AREA OF THE GULF. THE FRAGMENTS AS A WHOLE SPANNED AN AREA THAT WAS APPROXIMATELY 12.2NM BY 7.8NM. THE OIL APPEARED DARK AND WAS DISTINGUISHABLE FROM NATURAL PHENOMENA. THERE WERE A COUPLE POCKETS OF A SLIGHTLY LIGHTER HUE, WHICH MAY HAVE BEEN AN INDICATION OF RELATIVELY THICKER OIL. DUE TO THE FACTORS DESCRIBED ABOVE AND THE ASSOCIATION WITH THE HOTLINE, CONFIDENCE IN THIS REPORT WAS HIGH. WINDS AT THE TIME OF THE IMAGERY WERE S AT APPROXIMATELY 15KTS. TWO SEPARATE SECTIONS OF THE ANOMALY COULD BE SEEN IN THE SAR IMAGE. TOTAL LENGTH OF THE ANOMALY WAS 6.8 MILES WITH A MAXIMUM WIDTH OF 0.3 MILES. WHILE SEVERAL OIL FACILITIES ARE LOCATED NEARBY, IT CANNOT BE CERTAIN IF ANY ARE THE POINT SOURCE FOR THE POSSIBLE SLICK. UNCERTAINTIES: ANOMALY STANDS OUT WELL FROM THE SURROUNDING BACKGROUND AND HAS WELL DEFINED SHAPE, BOTH OF WHICH GIVE CONFIDENCE TO THE ANOMALY BEING OIL. HOWEVER WITHOUT A POINT SOURCE, CONFIDENCE WAS LIMITED TO MEDIUM. WHILE SEVERAL POINT SOURCES ARE NEARBY, WINDS WERE OUT OF THE NORTHEAST WHICH SUGGESTS THE POSSIBLE OIL HAD MOVED FROM NORTHEAST TO SOUTHWEST AND THUS WOULD NOT CORRESPOND TO THESE SOURCES.
